column1: # The shape of kernel/selinux/rules.c in each KernelSU fork, as our SUSFS
# reconciliations require it. Recorded on 2026-11-06, after the forks took
# tiann/KernelSU#3969.
# 2ca3db9, e2a9264), so its rules.c threads the generation now. Its #3964
# adaptation calls reset_avc_cache(seqno) through a local, to unify its three
# latest_granting arms (pol->, selinux_state.ss->, *latest_granting_ptr), and
# NOT reset_avc_cache(pol->latest_granting) as KSUN and SukiSU do -- so anchor
# and seqno_calls stay 0 here and no rules.c reconciliation moved. Verified on
# re-record: ksu_seqno_form() now reads 'upstream' and skips fix_selinux_seqno,
# that patch rejects at F0-F3 against the new file (which is what the seqno job
# asserts on the upstream arm), and verify_seqno()'s two
# selinux_status_update_policyload(0) checks pass -- all three publishers take
# the real seqno. The same push MOVED kernel/feature/selinux_hide.c into
# kernel/feature/selinux_hide/ and took #3981 with a third hook shape; that is
# a separate re-fit and this gate does not see it.
# anchor       occurrences of "reset_avc_cache(pol->latest_granting);" directly
#              followed by "out_unlock:" -- the insertion point both
#              next/susfs_fix_patches/*/fix_rules.c.patch and the SukiSu
#              builder's rules.c recovery use for susfs_set_batch_sid().
# bumps        occurrences of "latest_granting = old_pol->latest_granting + 1";
#              2 = the fork threads the real policy generation (#3964), so
#              apply_nomount_stack.sh classifies it 'upstream' and SKIPS
#              fix_selinux_seqno. 0 = the legacy seqno-less form.
# seqno_calls  reset_avc_cache(pol->latest_granting) call sites.
# legacy_calls seqno-less reset_avc_cache() call sites.
# A mismatch is upstream drift, not a bug here: it means a reconciliation may
# no longer apply. Re-fit the affected patch, THEN update the row.
# fork
KernelSU-Next
SukiSU-Ultra
BakaSU
